scope: Public snapshot resource/operation foundation and private runtime binding. Upstream comparison guides state ownership; it does not prove GoldenHoop public runtime support.

sources.observation: Persistent lifecycle/restore records are separate from API schemas and runtime objects; restore config retains backend ownership and resource limits.
sources.application: Store Snapshot is public; original runtime handle, opaque reference and execution candidates stay private worker metadata.

sources.observation: Slow runtime creation persists before worker submission; terminal state converges from actual runtime inspection, including read-time rechecking. Unsupported/preflight refusal is separate.
sources.application: Persist idempotent operation and source fence before dispatch. A durable dispatched marker is not Ready; uncertain dispatch is queried and never a fresh permit. Refusal before dispatch may release its fence; uncertainty after dispatch retains it.

sources.observation: Restore resolves server-owned persisted Ready state and owning backend, rather than accepting a caller-supplied artifact; preserved limits travel with the request.
sources.application: Public DTO must not accept private backend references or infer memory continuation from image-only restore. GoldenHoop still requires independent guest authority and explicit execution-ID binding.

validation: Initial production store/control strict targeted clippy passed. Five real SQLite tests pass after E0716 test-fixture borrow correction. Runtime source observations in database tests are synthetic; no actual public snapshot/backend acceptance.
